definitions: A language in which subject pronouns can be omitted from a sentence without making the sentence ungrammatical or ambiguous.
A language where the grammar allows for the omission of pronouns, especially subject pronouns, when they are recoverable from context.
examples: Spanish is a classic example of a pro-drop language.
In a pro-drop language, the verb conjugation often carries enough information to identify the subject.
Japanese is also considered a pro-drop language, though it extends beyond just subjects.
